claims.reason: Claims class / scope: the sentence names no program, so it must hold for every program in the job, but views_200.c, views_m1.c and views_321.c store 200, -1 and 321 in a. Needs 'views.c stores 66 in the int a.'

Maths: 66 = 0x42 = 01000010 and sizeof(int) is 4 here; the shift loop prints bits 7..0 and %#x prints 0x42. Holds for every program since it is about the value 66; 6.2.6.2 passages support the pure binary value bits.
Explanation: the d conversion passage says the int argument is converted to signed decimal; scoped to a = 66 and the run printed 66.

Overgeneralising: '(unsigned)a never changes a value' is false; the job's own views_m1.c shows (unsigned)-1 becoming 4294967295 (c.km1.u), and 6.3.1.3p1 only keeps values the new type can represent. The 'never' must be replaced with the condition (66 is representable in unsigned int).

Maths and mechanism check out: 66 is exact in double (6.3.1.4p2), 66 = 1.03125 x 2^6, biased exponent 1029 = 0x405, fraction 2^-5 gives 0x4050800000000000, matching the run; the binary64 statement is scoped to this machine and backed by the measured float.h values against EXAMPLE 2. Lines 15-18 are correctly described.

Mechanism: conversion to unsigned char (c passage) keeps 200 since it is in 0..255 on this machine; ASCII stops at 127 and terminal rendering is encoding-dependent. Run printed 200.
Maths: -1 + 2^32 = 4294967295, scoped to 32-bit unsigned int on this machine; 6.3.1.3p2 passage gives the add-one-more-than-max rule. Run printed -1 and 4294967295.
Maths: -1 + 256 = 255, scoped to this machine's unsigned char range; c and 6.3.1.3p2 passages support it. Run printed 255.
Maths: 321 = 256 + 65 = 0x141, low byte 01000001 = 0x41; value unchanged for %d and %u. Run lines 1-4 match.
Maths: 321 - 256 = 65, which is A in ASCII; scoped to this machine's unsigned char range; passages support the conversion. Run printed 65.
Mechanism: 66, 200, -1 and 321 are all exact in double (6.3.1.4p2) and %f with no precision gives six digits (f passage); the four captured runs match.

Claims class / scope: 'In memory, a is 4 bytes: 42 00 00 00' names no program, so it reads as true for every a in the job, but in views_200.c, views_m1.c and views_321.c a holds 200, -1 and 321. Needs 'In bytes.c' (or 'for a = 66'). The endianness part is correctly scoped to this machine.

Mechanism: '(double)a is a new object' is false; a cast yields a value, not an object. The object in bytes.c is d, which holds that value. Also the byte list and 8-byte size are platform facts (little-endian, sizeof(double) 8) with no 'on this machine' caveat, and no program is named.
